opportunity_thesis: The wrapper reuses idea 1's route, so build cost is small (INFERRED). The rail itself is cheap: the CDP facilitator's first 1,000 onchain transactions a month are free, then $0.001 each, and x402 serves human or machine buyers (OBSERVED, CDP docs). The gap is demand: no price, buyer or WTP exists (OBSERVED: 'No price number is set'), and the named buyers (T&S, brands) are reached 'through the API', which may mean contracts or keys rather than per-request wallets (INFERRED). The rail cannot run inside ChatGPT (OBSERVED, guidelines).
affected_user: Agent builders or T&S tools needing slang verdicts by API (SPECULATIVE).
economic_buyer: NOT_COMPUTABLE. For moderation vendors the payer may not be the beneficiary.
service_first_wedge: x402 wrapper on idea 1's GET /term/{slug}, test network only.
validation_path: V1: confirm one snapshot and route serve plugin and API.
V2 (desk): per named buyer type, write how it would pay: wallet or invoice/key.
V3 (Danny yes): list the route at a Danny-set price for a fixed window.
V4: count unaffiliated paid lookups and misses.
completion_proof: Settlement log with paid lookups from wallets Zero State does not control, inside the agreed window.
distribution: Not ChatGPT (obs-1). No open x402 hackathon found (OBSERVED). Agent-payment directories: NOT_COMPUTABLE.
failure_modes: buyer-rail mismatch; zero organic agent demand; open-sourcing the paid code via the hackathon; private-row leak

findings.summary: 'One build serves all three' conflicts with the hackathon rule that the entry calls Nebius Token Factory with an NVIDIA open model at runtime; a static lookup does not.
The hackathon requires a public open-source repo, so shared paid-API code would become freely reusable.

Paid demand is routed to x402, but the named payer (T&S teams) is reached 'through the API'. x402 does serve humans and machines (OBSERVED), so the open question is whether these buyers will pay per request from a wallet instead of by contract or key.
